golden-ratio.definition: The positive root φ = (1 + √5)/2 ≈ 1.6180339887 of x² − x − 1 = 0, satisfying φ² = φ + 1 and 1/φ = φ − 1.

golden-section.definition: A collinear point triple (A, G, B) whose consecutive segments stand in the golden ratio |AG|/|GB| = φ (so |AB|/|AG| = φ as well).

extreme-and-mean-ratio.definition: Euclid's classical definition: a straight line is cut in extreme and mean ratio when, as the whole line is to the greater segment, so is the greater to the less.

golden-chain.definition: A sequence of four or more collinear points in which overlapping triples form consecutive golden sections (such as lengths 1/φ, 1, 1/φ or 1, φ, φ²).

quadrance.definition: Norman Wildberger's Rational Trigonometry invariant measuring squared separation without square roots; two segments stand in ratio φ iff Q_long / Q_short = φ + 1 = φ².

geometrographie.definition: Émile Lemoine's 1902 operational metric counting elementary straightedge (R₁, R₂) and compass (C₁, C₂, C₃) operations; drawing a line through two points or a circle centered at one point through another each contributes simplicity 3.

vesica-piscis.definition: The symmetric lens formed by two congruent circles each passing through the other's center, generating √3 altitudes and bisecting their common radius.

mascheroni-construction.definition: A geometric construction using circles alone (0 straightedge lines), proved universal for all Euclidean constructible points by Georg Mohr (1672) and Lorenzo Mascheroni (1797).

rusty-compass.definition: A compass locked to a single invariant radius throughout a construction, studied by Abu'l-Wafa, Leonardo da Vinci, Poncelet, and Steiner.

power-of-a-point.definition: For a point P and circle O(r), the invariant quantity |PO|² − r², equal to the signed product |PA|·|PB| along any secant PAB (and to |PT|² along a tangent PT).

intersecting-chords-theorem.definition: If two chords AB and CD of a circle intersect internally at M, then |AM|·|MB| = |CM|·|MD|.

butterfly-theorem.translation: Crossed Cyclic Chords across a Midpoint Chord
butterfly-theorem.definition: Cyclic quadrilateral diagonals crossing a reference chord symmetrically, inducing projective cross-ratio and golden-section divisions.

kepler-triangle.definition: The unique right triangle whose side lengths (and side quadrances 1 : φ : φ²) form a geometric progression.

mixtilinear-incircle.definition: A circle internally tangent to two sides of a triangle and internally tangent to its circumcircle.

golden-rhombus.definition: A rhombus whose long and short diagonals stand in the golden ratio φ; thirty congruent golden rhombi bound Kepler's rhombic triacontahedron.

golden-rectangle.definition: A rectangle whose length-to-width ratio equals φ, characterized self-similarly by leaving a congruent-proportioned golden rectangle when a square gnomon is removed.
